doc.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Introduction and Turney's blues-inflected style
summary: Rowe introduces the interview and reads a description of Turney's alto style; Turney agrees and says the blues is his favorite sound.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Today we’re filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in Aspen Colorado at the Jerome Jazz Festival. I’m very pleased to have Norris Turney with me today, who is a saxophonist and woodwind player of much experience. I wanted to read something that a pretty well known jazz writer said about you in talking about your recordings and so forth. He said, “Norris Turney has a fine sound and style on alto sax, flute and clarinet. His alto combines swing era urgency and fluidity with bebop era exactness and technical expertise.” Do you agree with that?

Sure. Sounds like a pretty good write up to me. It seems like last night in your performance I heard — actually a bit of that stood out from some of the other players in my ears is that you had a lot of blues inflection in your playing but occasionally there were bebop licks too.
Yeah. Well I always liked the blues. Blues is my favorite sound, always has been.
